title: heap-buffer-overflow in fts3EvalUpdateCounts
live_proof: backport filter: upstream fix c7def600bd removes code still present in 3.22.0, and its own regression database reproduces on stock 3.22.0 under host ASan as heap-buffer-overflow in fts3EvalUpdateCounts
arena_bytes_why: 1 MiB on every arm. Five of the eight spatial cases are forced here by reachability -- at 262144 cases 21, 22 and 23 exhaust memsys5 before the defect (pcache1AllocPage dereferences the NULL that 3.22.0 does not check), 29 returns SQLITE_NOMEM, and 00 takes a different path -- so the same value is declared for all eight to keep the arms comparable. Measured 2026-10-17; this is also the value every recorded virtual reading was taken at, while CheriBSD had been running 262144.
object: the doclist fts3EvalUpdateCounts walks while accumulating matchinfo counts: pPhrase->doclist.pList, with its length in pPhrase->doclist.nList right beside it and never consulted. Measured 2026-10-16 by probe site 63: pList=0x2433c1 nList=3, and pList is an INTERIOR pointer, not a block base -- the doclist is a sub-range of a larger memsys5 block, which is what makes the address judgement too coarse to witness this case
lifetime_ender: not a lifetime defect: the walk runs past the end of the doclist on a corrupt image
shape: read past the end of the record
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: upstream's own regression image, run statement by statement through the in-domain memfs

The arms block is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-17 with one arena on every arm (arena_bytes=1048576) and every arm built from the corpus case.c: virtual-malloc MISSED, virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT cause=28 pc=0x3fb9a72e1c in fts3EvalUpdateCounts, cheribsd-revocation MISSED with RETURNED rc=0 and probe site 63 reporting hits=14 witnesses=2 -- reached and silent, not a no-reading. note: Re-measured 2026-10-16; every verdict holds and no count moves. The defect is a walk with no bound in it at all: fts3EvalUpdateCounts loops on while( 0xFE & (*p | c) ) and stops only at a zero byte, and pPhrase->doclist.nList -- the length, sitting in the same structure -- is never read. Two measured findings. (1) THE ADDRESS JUDGEMENT CANNOT WITNESS THIS CASE, and the reason is more fundamental than the reissue blindness recorded for cases 05 and 17. Site 63 prints pList=0x2433c1 nList=3: pList is an INTERIOR pointer, so the doclist is a sub-range of a larger memsys5 block rather than a block of its own, and the probe asks memsys5 which block an address belongs to and compares against THAT block's requested size. Reads a few bytes past a 3-byte doclist are still inside the enclosing block, so the probe reports hits=8 witnesses=0 on CheriBSD. That is the oracle's granularity being coarser than the object, and it is a fourth distinct form of the blind spot. It is NOT evidence that no over-read happened: nList=3 with eight walk iterations means at least five bytes were read past the doclist. (2) How FAR the walk runs is decided by the bytes that happen to follow, which is the spatial counterpart of case 20. On CheriBSD it met a zero byte after eight iterations and stopped while still inside the block, so that arm completes; on the Capstone Sublet image the following bytes were not zero, the walk left the block, and Sublet's bounds check fired with cause 28. Both arms without per-sub-allocation bounds are blind either way -- CheriBSD's revocation and bounds are at malloc granularity and the whole arena is one malloc -- so their silence is a genuine reached-and-silent, but the DISTANCE of the over-read is data-dependent and that is worth recording rather than treating the walk as bounded
fault_sites_why: Host ASan, running the same case source on stock 3.22.0, reports the invalid access in fts3EvalUpdateCounts (live_proof); that run is independent of the Capstone arms and predates them.
